record.paper_title: Stability of Homomorphisms, Coverings and Cocycles II: Examples, Applications and Open Problems
record.context_brief: bounded cocycle expanders with large cosystoles
record.original_question: Does there exist an infinite family of connected finite polygonal complexes {Xm} whose vertex degrees are uniformly bounded and for which the 0-dimensional and 1-dimensional cocycle Cheeger constants with permutation coefficients, together with the first cosystole with permutation coefficients, are all bounded below by the same positive constant λ, that is, h0(Xm, Sym), h1(Xm, Sym), and CoSyst1(Xm, Sym) are at least λ for all m?

evidence.quote:
Problem 6.6 (Bounded cocycle expanders with large cosystoles in permutations). Is there such a family for
which
∀m ∈ N : h0(Xm, Sym), h1(Xm, Sym), CoSyst1(Xm, Sym) ≥ λ,
where λ > 0 is independent of m?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be a connected finite 2-dimensional polygonal complex with vertex set V, edge set E, and 2-cell (polygon) set F. For n ∈ ℕ, let Sym(n) denote the symmetric group on n letters, regarded as a (non-abelian) coefficient system. A 0-cochain with permutation coefficients is a function f : V → Sym(n); a 1-cochain is a function g : E → Sym(n) (with each edge oriented). The coboundary of f is the 1-cochain (δ⁰f)(e) = f(e_+)·f(e_−)^{-1}, and the coboundary of g, viewed as a 2-cochain valued in Sym(n), is defined on each polygon σ as the ordered product of g along ∂σ. Define the (normalized Hamming) distance on cochains, and let B^i denote the i-coboundaries, Z^i the i-cocycles.

Define the cocycle Cheeger constants with permutation coefficients:
  h^0(X, Sym) = inf_n inf_{f : V → Sym(n), f ∉ B^0 (i.e. non-constant)}  ‖δ⁰f‖ / dist(f, B^0),
  h^1(X, Sym) = inf_n inf_{g : E → Sym(n), g ∉ Z^1} ‖δ¹g‖ / dist(g, Z^1),
and the first cosystole with permutation coefficients:
  CoSyst^1(X, Sym) = inf_n inf_{g ∈ Z^1 ∖ B^1} ‖g‖ (the minimum normalized weight of a nontrivial 1-cocycle, equivalently the minimum normalized distance from a non-cohomologically-trivial 1-cocycle to B^1).

Question: Does there exist an infinite family {X_m}_{m∈ℕ} of connected finite polygonal complexes with uniformly bounded vertex degrees and a constant λ > 0, independent of m, such that for every m,
   h^0(X_m, Sym) ≥ λ,   h^1(X_m, Sym) ≥ λ,   and   CoSyst^1(X_m, Sym) ≥ λ ?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears in a list of open problems on stability of homomorphisms and high-dimensional expansion with non-abelian (permutation) coefficients. No construction of such a family with uniformly bounded vertex degrees and simultaneous lower bounds on h^0, h^1, and CoSyst^1 in permutation coefficients has been reported. Related recent work studies cocycle stability of random 2-dimensional simplicial complexes in permutations but does not provide such an explicit bounded-degree family. Status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Cocycle stability in permutations of random simplicial complexes
status_evidence.snippet: Studies cocycle stability rate for random 2-dimensional Linial–Meshulam complexes with permutation coefficients; does not provide bounded-degree cocycle expanders with large cosystoles in permutations.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work addresses permutation cocycle stability for random complexes but does not resolve the bounded-degree question.

status_evidence.title: Bounded Degree Cosystolic Expanders of Every Dimension
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs bounded-degree cosystolic expanders with 𝔽₂ coefficients in every dimension.
status_evidence.claim: Bounded-degree cosystolic expanders are known with abelian coefficients, but the analogous question with permutation (non-abelian) coefficients is left open.
